messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: Multiple error-sampling gaps detected for our Sentry integration across prod and staging. Ingestion errors spike 03:12 UTC, rate of dropped events ~85%. Paging on-call SRE. :rotating_light:

maya: seeing the alerts, pulling up traces. Sentry DSN returns 502/504 intermittently, plus 429s. UI shows 'ingest backlog' for org redwood-prod.

oliver: tagged as sev-2? Customer-facing?

maya: starting triage — looks like our client SDK is getting 502s and our retry/backoff is causing a pileup. Some services are spiking error counts in our internal metrics (log-aggregator).

jack: i'm on-call. just saw the PD page. is this affecting user-facing errors or just telemetry?

maya: primarily telemetry—exceptions not arriving in Sentry so triage flow is impaired. BUT some of our product-side error-dashboard alerts are suppressing because they depend on Sentry-based alerts; that could delay customer impact detection.

arjun: on prod-api I can still see 5xxs in our own logs? any correlation?

maya: quick check: those 5xxs are unrelated app errors. Sentry not ingesting them, so triage is blind. Potential customer impact = slower detection + missing incident context for customers who rely on our error pages.

incident-bot: @jack — paging policy: page severity >= 2 to oncall. Notifying backups.

jack: OK. immediate mitigation steps I'm going to try: 1) reduce SDK sample rate on high-volume services to 0.1 (to reduce pressure) 2) enable local/file fallback for exception dumps to our internal logs 3) add temporary passthrough to internal ingestion queue so we can reprocess when vendor recovers. Will coordinate with eng teams.

liz: how do we toggle sample rate across services? we have a runtime flag?

oliver: yes, feature flags: toggles/sentry-sample-rate. i can roll to 0.1 for frontend-proxy, auth, upload-worker.

jack: oliver — please do that now. arjun, can you add a short-lived hook to write exceptions to our logs/redis queue when Sentry returns non-2xx? keep it gated behind a flag.

arjun: on it. i'll add the hook and a small sharded queue so we don't OOM. will push a canary to staging first.

maya: i'm opening a vendor support ticket and attaching traces. vendor-support: @Sentry support, we see 502/504/429 across multiple orgs starting ~03:12 UTC. ingestion errors high and consumers missing exceptions. any known region outage? token errors?

vendor-support: Thanks for the report. We're investigating an ingest pipeline degradation affecting EU and US-east. Tickets  #INC-45892 created. We're seeing backpressure from a dependent auth provider causing transient 502s. ETA unknown, will update in 10m.

jack: ok log a timeline: start mitigation 03:18 UTC - toggled sample rate to 0.1 for 3 highest-volume services. 03:21 UTC - enabled local fallback writing for exceptions on auth and proxy. 03:25 UTC - internal queue + reingest hook added to upload-worker canary.

oliver: sample-rate rollout complete to those services. will monitor error volume and token rates.

maya: i'm also updating the incident doc (internals/ops/incidents) with observed scope and mitigations — marking potential customer impact: delayed triage, missing breadcrumbs in support tickets for customers filing bugs since 03:12 UTC.

jack: reaching out to support leads for any active enterprise incidents that might be impacted. will coordinate comms if customers ask.

vendor-support: Update: upstream auth provider is throttling token validation; we're implementing a temporary token-caching layer to reduce auth calls. This should reduce 502s within ~20 mins.

maya: good. plan for reprocessing: once vendor clears, we'll re-push queued events from the internal queue to Sentry ingestion endpoint. we'll keep that gated and rate-limited to avoid overwhelming. arjun, ensure we have idempotency keys for replays.

arjun: yes — queued events will have original event_id and a replay flag. replayer will respect 10rps per project per minute.

jack: handoff — my shift ends in ~25m. @maya can you take primary until incident resolves? I'll remain reachable for escalation.

maya: taking primary. summarizing handoff in incident doc. If vendor doesn't confirm fix by 03:50 UTC escalate to vendor-SRE on-call and open an incident bridge.

incident-bot: REMINDER: scheduled on-call handoff in 20m for jack -> maya.

vendor-support: Update 03:44 UTC: auth provider reduced throttling; Sentry ingest retries decreasing; observed dropped events fall to ~12%. Full recovery expected in 15-30m. We're continuing to monitor.

maya: thanks. keep the replayer paused until we see sustained <5% drop for 10m. we'll then replay in controlled batches starting with non-customer-facing projects.

oliver: added a temporary dashboard tile in Console showing ingestion success rate and internal queue depth. keeping that up.

jack: final note before handoff: customers who filed issues between 03:12-03:45 may have missing exception context. Support should ask for logs or enable the support debug bundle until events are reprocessed.

maya: taking over. I'll keep updates in this thread and the incident doc. tagging @support-team for awareness.

vendor-support: 04:00 UTC: backend stabilized. ingest success >98% for last 5 minutes. We'll keep ticket open for post-mortem.

maya: confirming: observed success >98% for past 10m. internal queue drained to zero after controlled replays. closing this thread as mitigated. postmortem owner: oliver. action items captured in incident doc: - implement more robust SDK throttling/backoff, - add replay idempotency and better metrics, - add vendor outage alerting and fallback plan.

jack: thanks all. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: INCIDENT: resolved. Closing page.
